name: Vernal mercury

name: Roosevelt City Airport - Fuel Release
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting petroleum contaminated soils discovered during construction excavation near the airport fueling facility.  The excavation is only 3-feet deep and impacts to groundwater is unknown.  There are 2 above ground storage tanks, AV gas and jet fuel, nearby.

The contamination appears to be an old release and weathered.  They have contacted the Roosevelt City Manager, (Justin Johnson, 435-7220-5001) to inform them of the contaminated soil.  They are in the process of hiring a consultant to come collect samples and determine their next steps...

name: Newfield Water release

Workers were able to berm the drainage and recover ~55bbls of the water. Line was secured and the drainage will be flushed with approximately 250 bbls of fresh water which will be recovered. Soils samples to be collected next week for submittion to LHD.

name: Duchesne Co. - Two injection water spills
incident_summary: Caller reported two injection water spills into dry drainage ditches that occurred yesterday.  The first spill was 50 barrels at 6 a.m. and the second spill was 5 barrels at 7 a.m.  These occurred south of Myton about 3/4-miles apart from one another.  Caller said they will flush the impacted area with clean water and then sample the area for lab analysis.  GPS coordinates that caller provided did not provide a valid location on map; therefore, location on map is approximate.

name: Tri County - Production water release

Only surface soils were impacted; no waterways.  Clean-up is underway.

incident_summary: About 330 gallons of a corrosion inhibitor was spilled when a tote was broken.  The material is 30 percent methanol and was discharged into a tributary of the White River near Seven Sisters Road 0.5 miles south of Fiddler Road.  The district health department has been notified.  Their spill report with the MSDS of the material are attached.   The location map has been corrected and verified.  Coordiantes given are 40.01996, -109.38436.

name: Duchesne County Gycol Leak

The wellhead is UTE FEE 2-20C5, API 43-013-30550.

Caller reported a spill of 75-100 gallons of crude oil.  A leaking valve was discovered while loading a truck from tanks and the driver tried to off-load the crude, but the valve was off.  Oil impacted soils around the containment area.

name: Injection water spill near Myton
incident_summary: Internal pipeline corrosion caused 92 barrel loss of treated injection water. The water flowed 1395 feet down a drainage ditch to a sedimentation basin/cattle pond. The company will pump the pond dry, flush the pond and sample to ensure adequate cleanup.

name: Produced water release near Bonanza
incident_summary: A pipeline leak caused the release of 115 barrels of produced water. The affected soils will be scraped and the area flushed with clean water.

name: Production Water Spill
incident_summary: Spill report from EP Energy on pipeline from the Brotherson 3-23B4 to or past the Brotherson 2-23B4 WDW well into the central battery east of that site.  This line has been out of service for a few years and was tested or flushed yesterday with production water before moving Nabors Rig 561 in for a clean out and squeeze job, hoping to put this well back on production.  The line leaked in two places, one on location of the 2-23B4 WDW well and the other just south of that site along the pipeline right-of-way just west of the county road.  The first spill had been cleaned up before inspection this morning and the second one had not.  EP Energy estimated a 5 barrel spill at each leak site for a total of ten barrels.  The second release or leak site begins at GPS 559244E; 4460611N and runs north down slope to 559272E; 4460659N. Or about 144'.  Photos were taken.  Brent Brotherson owns the surface and the second spill might have left the right-or-way by ten or twenty feet. EP Energy was instructed to contact Brent Brotherson regarding the spill.

name: Hydrochloric Acid 28% Mix at Commercial Yard

Site crew deployed soda-ash.  Environmental cleanup contractor out of Salt Lake, Environmental Restoration, has been notified.  ETA 3 hours.  No impact to surface water or sewers.
title_eventname: Hydrochloric Acid 28% Mix at Commercial Yard

The well name is Cige 20. It did get into a dry wash (Cottonwood Wash) but contained there. Most of the contaminated soil has been removed and they are in the process of removing the rest. name: LCL Oil Co. (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: LCL tanker was delivering fuel to a small farm type elevated tank on legs and in a field.  After completing the delivery, the tank truck pulled away from the tank pad, but the slick muddy base under the wheels allowed the truck to slide sideways and the truck pulled off the standing tanks outlet valve.  The driver ran over to the tank and placed his hand over the hole thus limiting the total spill to 174 gallons of diesel fuel.  The driver kept the hole plugged until the local FD and others arrived to mitigate.  No diesel entered a storm drain or any other state waters.  A contractor called in by LCL had a vac truck suck up spilled fuel and also the affected soils have been excavated and will be hauled to the Harmaston Bench solid waste disposal facility.  Absorbent pads were also used to mitigate the spill.  Darrin Brown of the local health department has inspected the site and monitored the clean-up operations.  He will follow-up with a final inspection.

name: Unknown (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller witnessed white tanker trucks dumping an unknown liquid substance into what he referred to as "Kids" canal at 1500 West near 500 South (behind a movie theater complex).  He saw trucks doing this on at least two occasions: Thursday (Oct 16) at 6:30 pm and again the next day Friday (Oct. 17) at 12:30 pm. Caller is reporting a recurring hydrogen sulfide gas odor.A at her home that is likely coming from a nearby blue bench disposal extraction well.

The injection well was not in use at the time, but the thief hatches on tanks for both oil wells north and south of the house were leaking.  He left a card with Greg. I called Nathan on his cell and left a message.    Also, called Duchesne County after hours number and they said the would contact Mrs. Pilling tonight.

Mrs. Pilling called back and indicated the wind has shifted directions and they are able to breathe again and the odors have subsided.

name: Anadarko NBU 922-31N
incident_summary:
Yesterday at approximately 12:00 pm a tank leak was discovered at the NBU 922-31N location.  A condensate/water tank developed a hole in the bottom due to corrosion which lead to the release of 295 bbls.  290 bbls were recovered inside of the secondary containment.  There appeared to be a bent area in the northwest corner of the steel containment where approximately 5 bbls leaked out side of the secondary containment berm.  2 bbls of produced water seeped through the location and ran approximately 700 ft. down a dry drainage.  All released product was recovered except the 2 bbls that left location and due to the terrain and steepness of the area it was not possible to recover the released produced water.  Out of the 295 bbls release there were approximately 2 bbls of condensate that were contained inside of the secondary containment.  
 
The cleanup for this release started at 12:30 pm.  West Rock was able to control and contain the produced water that was leaking out of the damaged portion of the containment.  They were also able to stop the produced water from seeping through and leaving location.  Savage was able to drain out everything inside of the secondary containment and haul it for disposal.  All liquid and contaminated soil outside of the secondary containment is being collected and taken off for disposal.  All tanks were closed and drained so no farther produced can be released.

name: Roosevelt Manure Truck wahsout to creek
incident_summary:
Attached is the email report submitted by Scott Hacking
Darrin and I witnessed this incident firsthand late yesterday, at approximately 4:30pm.  Photos with captions are at:
https://picasaweb.google.com/105377044848809547245/WintertonTruckingSpill?authuser=0&authkey=Gv1sRgCIfr7LCw8tmdCw&feat=directlink
Attached is a Google Earth placemark showing the location.  This occurred on a small tributary to Dry Gulch Creek, just west of Roosevelt.  Darrin and I were driving by on US-40 approximately 4:30pm yesterday (June 5th) when we saw a cattle hauling truck to the north of the highway that had backed up to the small creek and was obviously being washed out.  We turned off the highway to investigate and found that a Winterton Trucking cattle hauling truck was in the process of being washed out into the small creek (see photos).  The water coming out of the truck was heavily laden with manure and it was inundating the small creek with manure and probably ammonia also (from the urine).  We observed dead and dying minnows in the small creek directly downstream of this, where the small creek was choked with manure.  We talked to a representative of the trucking company that was present and told them this activity was not allowed, and they agreed to stop the activity.  Apparently there had been several cattle trucks washed out at this location over the course of several days, in addition to the truck we observed being washed out.

No water samples were taken, as it did not seem necessary given the firsthand observations.  Any sample collected would have contained a heavy fraction of solids, due to the heavy manure load in the creek that this event caused.  The creek immediately downstream was more of a manure slurry than water.  I think we could sample this location for weeks to come and see the negative effects.  Please advise if you want us to do that.

Wintertons do own the land where this incident occurred.  It is open to public access, and there are no gates; there is direct access off of US-40.

As you know, Darrin sent an email earlier today recommending an NOV for this incident, and I agree completely.  Downstream this incident probably killed on the order of a hundred minnows, and it will negatively impact the creek for some time to come.  The amount of manure being washed out totally overwhelmed the small creek, and it will probably be many months before the Creek and its associated ecosystem can recover.  This was also a very blatant incident, occurring adjacent to the Roosevelt City Limits and only about 150-200 yards off of US-40.
title_eventname: Roosevelt Manure Truck wahsout to creek

name: Quality Inspection & Testing, Inc. (Null RP Substituted)

Caller reported a that a truck hauling radioactive material overturned along Highway 40.  Initial reports indicate that the material breached the containment.  An unknown liquid and powder material surrounds the crash site and EMS workers may have come into contact with these materials.  Jeremy Raymond (Uintah County Fire Dept.) is on-scene and awaiting meters (Geiger counters) to survey the area.  DERR contacted Bill Craig (Division Radiation Control - DRC).

UPDATE 1 10/24/10 08:54:  Bill Craig (DRC) reported that the truck rolled just west of Vernal on Highway 40.  The radiation source did NOT breach containment and there are NO exposures resulting from the incident.  The radiation source is owned by Quality Testing and they are on-scene working with local Emergency personnel.  The source is Iridium 192 and is intact.  I do not have the destination information for the source but the radiation source is a device used for strength-testing metals in production wells and welds in other metal components. Bill indicated these devices and their radiation sources are designed and secured during transport to withstand high impacts during accidents.  The driver of the truck was reportedly drunk at the time of the crash and he was removed from the scene by ambulance to treat injuries from the accident but was not exposed to any radiation. Bill Craig (801) 565-1129 (home phone) has been in contact technical support and providing with the On-Scene Coordinator - Duchesne Fire Chief Jeremy Raymond.  Gwen Galloway (DRC) home phone: (801) 964-2035 has taken over technical support duties and may visit the scene later today to provide regulatory oversight for handling of the source.  All indications are that the situation is now under control.

UPDATE 2 10/24/10 10:02:  Liquid material involved in the spill appears to be a dilute bleach solution used in the development of images taken by the device.  A contractor was hired to provide clean-up of the solution as well as any diesel released during the accident.

incident_summary:
Small amounts of mercury were discovered on the parking lot and sidewalk at the Vernal Middle School.  Cause is unknown.  Local Health Dept. and Fire Dept. have responded.

Response: I have contacted the EPA who in turn will talk to the Tri County Health Dept. about the situation.  If necessary, the EPA will hire their contractor -E.R.- to perform the cleanup.

09:12 TRI-County contacted DEQ again after learning of the possibility and availability of a mercury vapor meter.  
DERR sent some preliminary documentation with mercury info to the health dept.

10:20 Tri-County informed DEQ that an EPA OSC will mobilize to the school to render assistance.  Tri-County is currently evacuating the school.  Free mercury was not observed at the entrances used by students.  Free mercury was believed observed near where the cooks enter the kitchen.

11:30 by JD Keetley: Craig Meyers (303-312-7166), OSC with EPA, informed me that he has sent the EPA responder, David Romero (303-884-1236) to Vernal along with the EPA contractor, URS.  They are driving to Vernal from Denver and should arrive there in a few hours.  Any questions on the response can be taken up with them.  I’ll update things as necessary. – JD

8/25/06 Update by JD Keetley: The EPA and contractor URS arrived in Vernal Thursday night and the cleanup is underway.

Friday morning (8/25/06) I received an inquiry from Richard Gee with State Public Safety and Darren Brown with Tri-County Health Department regarding State regulations or guidelines for the cleanup of mercury inside the Vernal school.  I told them we have guidelines that are based on the U.S. EPA’s guidelines taken off their website.

After conferring with other DERR personnel and with SLVHD personnel who have had experience with similar situations, I called back Darren Brown and advised that the usual cleanup level for mercury in ambient air is 3,000 nanograms/cubic meter for a commercial building and 1,000 nanograms/cubic meter for a residential building.  I added that a public school would be better off to make the cleanup level 1,000 nanograms (1 microgram).

Darren told me they had already made that decision and were going ahead with that cleanup level in mind.  He said the highest readings on their Lumex machine have been around 400 - 500 nanograms and that staying under 1,000 nanograms should not be that difficult.

There was still some uncertainty as to whether the cleanup would address the cafeteria workers who had possibly tracked the mercury onto their shoes and into their cars and homes.  If the EPA demobilizes after cleaning up the school only, then the Tri-County Health Department would be left to handle the monitoring and cleanup of the workers’ personal clothing and homes.  Since the County does not have a Lumex meter, they would ask DERR’s assistance in doing this since we do have a Lumex meter and trained personnel to use it.

As of 11:00 am Friday, no decision has yet been reached regarding the potential cafeteria workers’ mercury contamination.  -  JDK

Update & Summary 8/29/06: Thursday, August 24, 2006:  Mercury contamination was discovered in the parking and inside the building at the Vernal Middle School due to an anonymous phone call in the morning.  All students, faculty, and staff were dismissed from the school.

Initial notification of the incident to UDEQ/DERR was received Thursday morning around 8:30.  The situation was discussed with both Richard Gee at Utah DES and Darren Brown with Tri-County Health Department.  At 9:00 am, Craig Meyers with the U.S. EPA was contacted.  Craig later informed that he had mobilized their contractor, URS, and his field OSC, Dave Romero, to go to the site.  They arrived in Vernal late in the afternoon and began initial assessment and cleanup of the site.

It was estimated about 3 tablespoons of mercury had been spilled outside in the parking lot, and school employees later tracked the mercury into the building.  Mercury vapors were detected inside the school building.  The contractor ventilated the building, began clean up the mercury using special vacuums, and prepared to remove the contaminated flooring and carpets if necessary.

Friday August 25:  Cleanup levels for the mercury spill were discussed.  An “action level” of 1,000 nanograms/cubic meter (n-gm/m3 or 10-9 gm/m3) of mercury vapor in the air was set.  The contractor used a Lumex meter to measure mercury levels as cleanup of the school interior and the outside parking lots and sidewalks progressed.  Most levels inside the school were found to be less than 500 n-gm/m3, while outside levels of 1,000+ n-gm/m3were measured.

School was still not in session during the cleanup.  Meanwhile, the State DOH and the Utah Poison Control Center had been getting calls from concerned parents and doctors in Vernal about the spill.  The issue of the cafeteria workers’ possible mercury contamination on their clothes, homes, or cars was brought up.  In the afternoon, the EPA, the URS contractor, and the Tri-County Health Department offered employees of the school who feel they may have come into contact with mercury to have their clothes, shoes, cars, etc tested for mercury.  It was a voluntary offer, and EPA/URS would be in town all day Friday for it.  One employee came to be tested, and had her car tested for mercury levels.  The car’s levels were below action levels.  It was felt this car was the one most likely to have been exposed to mercury since it had been parked in the area of the spill in the parking lot.

By Friday evening, the cleanup was mostly over.  All contaminated materials were placed in bags and secured for the weekend.  The contractor continued to ventilate the school overnight and planned to come back in the morning to test the ambient air levels.  

Saturday August 26:  When the contractor returned to the school in the morning, the highest level of mercury measured was 250 n-gm/m3, found in the janitor’s closet due to an initial attempt to cleanup the spill himself.  Throughout the rest of the building, all rooms were tested and found to be at acceptable levels.  Outside, levels of 1,000 n-gm/m3 were still detected so the contractor applied MercEx (?) to the sidewalk: sprinkling finely powdered sulfur or zinc on the spill site to bind any remaining mercury so it can no longer vaporize.  All cracks and crevices in the sidewalks were then sealed with caulking.  When the sidewalks were tested again, results showed levels below 200 n-gm/m3.

The EPA and URS returned to Denver Saturday afternoon.  The contaminated materials from the cleanup were double-bagged and placed in a steel container which was later moved to a vacant, secure 5-acre lot owned by the Health Department.  The contractor took samples of the contaminated material to deliver to a laboratory in Steamboat Springs, Colorado, for analysis to determine if the material is hazardous.  When results come back, URS will return to Vernal to retrieve the container and dispose of it in an appropriate landfill: either Subtitle C or D depending if the material is deemed hazardous or not.  The material will be hauled off within a week.

Monday August 28:  Health Department personnel met with school officials and verified that everyone is satisfied with the cleanup.  School is back in session and there are no further issues of concern.

For any further information on this incident, please contact J. D. Keetley with UDEQ at 801-536-4130 or at jkeetley@utah.gov

name: EP Energy, Brine Release,
incident_summary:
Late Wednesday evening a call came in from a land owner that he had found a salt water leak on his property, the night lease operator and production supervisor met with the land owner and went to the location and found the salt water line south of the Brotherson 2-15B4 had developed a leak 2000 feet south of the location.
The leak was in the crossing of a dry wash, the water ran 150 yards down the wash and was contained in a catch basin.
The pipe line is a 2 7/8 steel line wrapped with black tape and fiberglass lined.
The line was exposed and found to have external corrosion.
The line will be repaired and hydro tested.
Calculator 5 and 6 was used.
90 bbls was spilled

Line break spill point GPS:  557199E; 4461018N
Wash berm or end point:     557297E; 4461049N
(berm or dam constructed by surface owner to catch rainwater)


Photos of spill indicate backwash fluid level was several feet above the bottom of the wash some thirty feet west of the line break or spill, which leaves me to believe the volume of water is much higher than reported.  The landowner told the operator there was water already in the bermed area below from the rains and so EP Energy reduced their original report of 300 barrels to 90.  I believe the operator did recover three loads of spill or spill/rainwater from the bermed area below which was between 240 to 300 barrels of fluid.  There was no trace of oil in the spill area.  When Scott Hacking and I returned on a second visit the bermed area still had six inches of fluid or more, which either was left or was water that had drained from the saturated soils of the wash.  The landowner was contacted and EP Energy promised to send DOGM a contact number.  The operator explained that the landowner claimed a spring was present in that wash, but I could not find a (for sure) stream flow at any point and would have to make another trip after the wash drys out.

name: Book Cliffs Pipeline Release
incident_summary:
Hector Monteroso noticed the spill when driving along the county road to his lease on another parcel of trust land.  The easement for the pipeline is held by Slate River Resources, LLC, 418 E Main, Vernal, 84078.  The easement was approved in February of 2006.  It is described as an 8-inch natural gas gathering pipeline that transports gas from wells in the Agency Draw area to market.  It crosses trust land in Section 2, T13S, R20E, and terminates in Section 35, T12S, R20E, where it connects to another pipeline.

David Hackford of DOGM visited the site Tuesday morning at approximately 9am, and he reported that the 8-inch diameter pipeline was leaking a small amount of natural gas under relatively low pressure, and that some condensate liquids had leaked out of the pipeline and covered a small area of ground near the pipeline.  Dave called Slate River's contractor (the "pumper", not sure who that was) and told them to fix the leak ASAP.  

SITLA staff (Sonja Wallace, Jim Davis and Scott Bartlett) and I also visited the site at approximately 11:30am on Tuesday, and found things as Dave had described.  The contractor had not responded yet to fix the leak, but it was raining at the time and weather was a factor in getting equipment to the scene.  The leak was small and not too serious, due to the low pressure in the line at the time.  The condensate spill was very localized, as Dave had described.  We did not collect any samples due to the very localized nature of the condensate spill, which had only run about 5 or 6 feet from the pipeline.  The spill is small and should be very easy to clean up.

Surface water was not affected, the nearest would be Willow Creek, which is over 3 miles away from this location.  It was raining at the time, so there was some stormwater runoff.

name: Elpaso Energy (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
From John Isanhart USFS 11/8/11:   Looks like it is mostly cleaned up. The pit has oil in it with a lot of cellulose. It really only went between the well head and pit.. No signs of spillage outside of the pad area. This is a fee well so our jurisdiction is just mig birds and other listed fish or animals. The only listed species in the near vicinity would be Ute's ladies tresses. There are some wetland areas along the road into the well but not next to the pad itself.

The well is in the NENW Sec 3 T 2 S R 3 W. It is labelled the Conover 3-3B-3. 

Update From Scott Hacking:  11/5/2011 - I was at the site today at noon.  El Paso was right in the middle of critical operations to contain the well, so I was not able to get too close to the well head (still a threat of explosion, H2S gas present).  The well was still uncontained but oil was not really shooting up in the air, the oil had been diverted to flow to excavated ponds on site.  As far as I could tell oil was not leaving the site.  El Paso did have a stream of trucks coming and going to truck the oil out of the emergency pits that had been constructed at the site.  The nearest downstream surface water is a farmer's pond about 1/4 mile away.  The first "live" water is about two miles SE downstream (Dry Gulch Creek, which does have water at this location).  There is also a pond that is closer to the NW but that pond is uphill from the site.  The irrigation season is over so the farmer's ditches and the canals do have water in them currently.  It is unknown how deep the groundwater is at the site, but apparently they did not hit groundwater while excavating the emergency ponds.  Dwayne Davies with El Paso is the contact for this incident, he was at the site but was extremely busy with operations to cap the well.  His mobile phone is 435-823-1470, and his e-mail is dwayne.davies@elpaso.com.  EPA was not at the site yet when I was there.  The local incident command system has not been activated, El Paso is in control of the site and has the resources to address the situation.  They have established access control at the site and appear to be dealing with the situation appropriately and with urgency.  A well control company (Wild Well Control) has been brought in to help them deal with the situation.  
 
El Paso has multiple H2S meters at the site and on their personnel.  The nearest neighbor is about 1/8 mile to the west (see photo 16 in background), which is generally upwind but not always (today the wind was blowing stiffly to the east so that neighbor was upwind).  The next nearest potentially downwind neighbor is about 1/4 mile to the NE (see photo 15, the residence is on the right).  There are two other residences to the NW and SW slightly further away.  There did not appear to be anybody home at the two closest residences, they may have been advised to leave by Mike Lefler (local Fire Marshall), but I am not sure about that.  
 
So there appears to be no release to surface water at this time.  There is still some potential for H2S gas release, but measurements so far at the site (according to El Paso) have been low.  The wind is helping disperse H2S from the immediate area.  We should revisit the site Monday or Tuesday (hopefully the well is fully contained by then) for more detailed followup and to determine for sure if the excavated ponds encountered any groundwater.  I don't forsee that water sampling will be needed unless we find out GW was impacted at the site.
 
 - Scott

name: Production Water Spill
incident_summary:
This spill was reported to DERR via email from Scott Hacking.  The spill was originally reported to the Utah Division of Oil, Gas and Mining (DOGM) on Monday, March 31, 2014 by Scott Ghan with Bill Barrett Corp.  Scott Ghan reported that a pipeline break surfaced leaving the UDWR 14-29-36 BTR well to the west, approximately sixty to seventy yards down that pipeline and then ran down across the access road and then north into a winter range field owned by the Division of Wildlife Resources (DWR).  Scott Gahn estimated they lost more than a hundred barrels of production water.  Besides DOGM, he notified the DWR and since the minerals are Tribal, the Tribe was also notified.  Because of DOGM's hundred barrel or major event rule, Scott Gahn notified DOGM immediately about this spill event.

David Hackford of DOGM visited the site Tuesday morning at approximately 9am, and he reported that the 8-inch diameter pipeline was leaking a small amount of natural gas under relatively low pressure, and that some condensate liquids had leaked out of the pipeline and covered a small area of ground near the pipeline. We did not collect any samples due to the very localized nature of the condensate spill, which had only run about 5 or 6 feet from the pipeline.  The spill is small and should be very easy to clean up.

Surface water was not affected, the nearest would be Willow Creek, which is over 3 miles away from this location.  It was raining at the time, so there was some stormwater runoff.

Darrin knows about this spill, he was going to join us for our site visit but had another commitment at the time.

The easement for the pipeline is held by Slate River Resources, LLC, 418 E Main, Vernal, 84078.  The easement was approved in February of 2006.  It is described as an 8-inch natural gas gathering pipeline that transports gas from wells in the Agency Draw area to market.  It crosses trust land in Section 2, T13S, R20E, and terminates in Section 35, T12S, R20E, where it connects to another pipeline.

Because of the rain, some of the spill (less than 5 barrels) was flushed onto tribal lands.  Caller said that the impacted area is being flushed and vacuumed to retrieve as much production water as possible but the area is muddy so clean-up has been difficult.

name: Peck  Rock (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Caller reports the repeated dumping of some type of hazardous waste in a pit less than 100 yards west of the address location in the Peck Rock facility..  The local fire department has been on-site and conducted some of field tests.  The local health department has also been on-site but the dumping reportedly continues.  A strong chemical smell comes into their home.

Update---From NRC report and EPA OSC  Steven Way ---Several people have gone to doctors and the hospital as result of exposure to the chemical smell.  The mayor and 911 system has been used several times by many people in the neighborhood.  

The fire marshal ( Tam Hay) indicates that he went to the site last weekend.  He says the smell starts about 8:30 p.m. and stings your eyes and throat.  He says the smell is quite strong.

The local health department and the fire marshal requested that we bring in EPA to provide a more robust monitoring capability.  We (Dale, Brent, Neil) have coordinated this request for EPA assistance with Matt Sullivan with the Division of Solid and Hazardous Waste because a possible source of the smell is a nearby construction landfill (Peck Rock).  He will be the point person with EPA. 

The EPA in responding OSC will be Al Lange.  He should be here within 24 hours.

Ralph Bohn with the Division of Solid and Hazardous Waste visited the landfill on the evening of August 3.  He reports that there appears to be a fire in the working face of the landfill.  Al Lange will be on site by the evening of August 4.

Update - Matt Sullivan will be joining the EPA OSC and representatives from the Utah County Health Department to visit the Peck Rock landfill this evening.  The landfill owner will be given an opportunity to develop a plan to identify and extinguish the landfill fire.  EPA resources will likely be available if the landfill owner does not have the capability.

Ralph Bohn indicates that there is a very strong smell of fire downwind of the landfill.  It is not a chemical smell.  The fire is not visually observable.

name: Duchesne -- Produced water spill
incident_summary: A seal in the pump in the salt water line inside the pump house failed, releasing an estimated 23 barrels of produced water.  The discharge was confined by the containment berm and did not leave the pad or enter the environment.  Vacuum trucks recovered an estimated 5 barrels.

name: Ethylene Glycol Release
incident_summary:
Caller reported that 1030 gallons of ethylene glycol were released at a well site approximately 8 to 10 miles southwest of Myton.  The RQ for ethylene glycol is 5000 pounds.  The caller reported that it weighs 9.29 pounds per gallon making the release over 9568 pounds.

The glycol ran off the well site and down a road and into a dry drainage, there was no water in the drainage at the time.  It then flowed approximately 150 feet down the drainage.  Approximately 200 gallons entered the drainage.  The drainage was dammed and the flow stopped.  They used a pump truck to suck up all the liquid in the drainage then began to remove the contaminated soil.  The soil will be stockpiled at the well site then transferred to Environmental Energy Inovations where it will be remediated.

The well site was number 8-33-8-16 and is located south east of the north east quarter quarter of section 33, 8 south 16 east.

name: Oil Production Produced Water Spill - Roosevelt
incident_summary: CALLER CONTACTED NRC AND REPORTED THAT PRODUCED WATER FROM A WELL POND IS RUNNING DOWN INTO A WASH. CALLER IS CONCERNED ABOUT WELL WATER CONTAMINATION.  THE OWNER/OPERATOR MAY BE RN INDUSTRY BLUEBELL DISPOSAL.
title_eventname: Oil Production Produced Water Spill - Roosevelt

name: Uintah County -- Methanol release
incident_summary: A valve broke loose on a pipeline, releasing an estimated 40 barrels of methanol into a lined berm that was filled with snow.  No waterways impacted.  Snow/methanol mixture was recovered.

name: Duchesne Diesel Release
incident_summary: Caller reported that the Pilot/Flying J truck was heading West on US 40 near mm 83 when it was involved in a near head on collision with water truck. The accident resulted in the release of ~100 gallons of diesel fuel from the saddle tanks on the truck and about 10 gallons of DEF. Release was reported to have only been to road surface, and was addressed by emergency response personnel. There was not report of impact to surface waters.

name: Uintah County -- Produced water release
incident_summary: Operator discovered a release of an estimated 15 barrels of produced water from a corroded section of line which had failed.  The release was fully contained on location.

name: Uintah County Produced Water Release
incident_summary:
The caller reported that approximately 30 barrels of produced water were released at a water injection well site number WV50.  The coordinates of the site are: Latitude: 40.12528, Longitude: -109.53812.

The cause of the release was a cow rubbing the handle on a ball valve that opened the valve.  The valve has been closed and the handle removed to prevent incidents like this in the future.

All water was contained to the site and has been collected and taken to a disposal well.  There were no threats to any water bodies.

name: Myton - Treated Injection Water release
incident_summary:
Caller reported a leak in an underground pipeline resulted in the release of 15 barrels (bbls) of treated injection water. The release surfaced and 10 bbls remained on the well site and 5 bbls released off-site into a dry drainage. Line will be repaired.

Lat/Long Coordinates 40°2'37.17" North/109°59'40.54" West

name: UPDATE Duchesne County -- Crude oil mist
incident_summary:
A drilling rig experienced a blowout, which created a fine mist of crude oil that fell onto the surface of the pad.  A small amount floated down onto the neighboring property.  The ground was mostly covered with snow at the time and there was no free-flowing liquid crude oil observed on the surface.  No waterways have been impacted.  Estimated total of oil is 6 barrels.  Crews began cleanup on 22 Dec 17.

Report has been updated with accurate location.
title_eventname: UPDATE Duchesne County -- Crude oil mist

name: Randlett --Crude Oil Spill
incident_summary: Reporting party states an unknown quantity of crude oil leaked from a well onto the ground and into a nearby pond, possibly affecting vegetation and wildlife.  Incident is believed to have occurred in January, 2019 and was not discovered until 2 Apr 19.  Report is late due to a breakdown in communication.

name: Vernal - Hydraulic oil spill
incident_summary: Caller reported an estimated 150 gallon hydraulic oil release to soil due to broken machinery.  No waterways were impacted.  The soil will be cleaned up when the machinery can be moved.

name: Uintah Co - Diesel Spill 50 Gallons
incident_summary: Caller is reporting the release of a (rough) estimate volume of 50 gallons of diesel to soils from a vehicle used in the mining process to mix diesel with ammonium nitrate.  A check-valve leaked to soils.  The entire work area is contained within earthen dam.  Will clean up and process through facility.  Facility will plans to make a more precise determination of the amount released.   No surface waters or drains were impacted.

name: Western Petroleum (Joey Cupp) (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported approximately 100 gallons of diesel was released when an above ground storage tank (AST) was overfilled.  Release was due to operator error.  Company initially believed the AST was installed inside concrete containment system and sent a vac-truck to recover the diesel.  Vac-truck driver observed that the AST did not have concrete containment and that the release had seeped into the surrounding soils.  Remedial activities will proceed to address contaminated soils.

name: Roosevelt ITL Production Water Dumping.
incident_summary:
Forwarding a complaint sent to DOGM by EP Energy from a lady who lives in Duchesne County. The complaint detailed a driver for Iowa Tank Lines truck who was seen and photographed dumping production water into the wash bed on Saturday, March 15th.  The complaint has photos of the truck and numbers at the time of the dumping but has not forwarded them as yet; the complainant claims that he dumped water on the road in the past that had oil in it.

The spill site is at 0577975E; 4465337N and immediately off the right or east side of the road into the lower of the wash.  The wash bottom is fine-grained sand so it is hard to determine how much water was dumped, but it did run down the wash over a hundred feet, a wash that has several low areas that would puddle until the water evaporates or subs away.  I will forward another email when I receive the photos and the offenders name and truck information.

name: Uintah County/sump sludge
incident_summary: Ashley upper canal workers went to work on a canal outlet and discovered someone had dumped sludge around the concrete lateral exiting the canal. A recent dump occurred with in the last 24 hours, but previous loads have been dumped there. Gray and black in color and odorous. fifty feet from a resident. Dump occurred on Millecan's property. They are out of town on vacation.

name: Used Engine Gear Oil Spill
incident_summary: 330 Gallon tote of used drilling rig engine gear oil was being off-loaded with a fork-lift for transfer to a facility used oil tank.  The tote slipped off the forks, tipped and spilled.   Incident occurred within a concrete and asphalt and bermed containment area.  An estimated five to ten gallons splashed to soils outside of the containment.    Cleanup is underway.  As of this time upwards of 200 gallons have been recovered.    Absorbents and floor-dry have been deployed.  Contaminated soils are being excavated and drummed for disposal.   No impact to surface waters or sewers.

name: 50 Gallons Hydraulic Spill at Simplot
incident_summary: A hose on a loader broke spilling 30-50 gallons of hydraulic oil to the soil. The soil will be excavated and hauled off for disposal.

name: Duchesne County Treated Injection Water Release
incident_summary:
The caller reported that a buried, steel pipeline leaked 107 barrels of treated injection water that ran off the well site and into a dry drainage.  It flowed down the drainage and into a stock water pond that was full to capacity causing the pond to breach and allowing the injection water and contaminated stock water to flow approximately 5049 additional feet down the dry drainage.

The well number is 22-6-9-17.

The line has been shut in and isolated.

No water bodies besides the stock pond were impacted.

Clean up will include removing all contaminated water from the pond and flushing the pond and drainage with approximately 200 barrels of fresh water.  Nathan Hall is overseeing the clean up.
title_eventname: Duchesne County Treated Injection Water Release

name: Roosevelt - Condensate release
incident_summary: Caller reported that a truck rollover resulted in the release of 5-7 bbls. condensate.  Rollover caused a valve on the truck to open, resulting in the release.  Responsible party is awaiting Blue Stakes clearance before excavating impacted soils.  Responsible party agreed to provide a clean-up report to the Tri-County Health Department within 30 days.

name: Uinta County - Hydraulic Oil Spill
incident_summary: Caller reported a spill of approximately 85-90 gallons of hydraulic fluid from a 1.5" hydraulic line on Hitachi EX18 shovel.  Release occurred in one of the pits.  Crew shut down the equipment.  After shovel is repaired they will walk it off the area of impact to perform cleanup.  No impact to surface waters.  Facility has 100 ton haul truck to which they deposit excavating contaminated soils.  When full that will be delivered to Uinta County Landfill for disposal.

name: Vernal - Hydraulic oil release at Simplot
incident_summary: Caller reported that a hydraulic line on a rotary drill rig ruptured releasing an unknown quantity of hydraulic oil (current best guess estimate is 50-75 gallons).  Once the line is repaired and the oil reservoir tank is refilled, the released quantity will be determined.  The release impacted the overburden soils beneath the drill rig before two small plastic swimming pools could be placed as temporary secondary containment to contain the release.
title_eventname: Vernal - Hydraulic oil release at Simplot

name: Altamont - Used oil release
incident_summary: Caller reported a 3.7 gallon used oil spill to a dry creek bed.  The spill had been cleaned up at the time of the call to DERR.  Caller said the contaminated dirt was taken to IWM disposal site.  Caller reported the spill to DOGM.

name: Duchesne County - Treated Injection Water
incident_summary:
Caller reported a release of 145 barrels of treated injection water that ran off the right-of-way into a dry drainage ditch. Clean-up is underway with the line currently isolated. Completion of the repair is planned for Monday, July 10, 2017. No waterways were impacted. 

Caller also contacted Nathan Hall with DEQ, Amy Doebele with DOGM, and Randy Bywater with the BLM.

name: Levi Smuin (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reports a release of approximately 50 gallons of unleaded gasoline at facility fueling island.  Operator started fueling and left the process unattended.  (purchase was for 64.2 gallons).  Fuel flowed into and was completed contained in a concrete drain (drain flows to grass, which was not impacted).  On-site personnel immediately deployed absorbant onto the fuel.  Naples Fire Dept. responded.  As a result of the quick response by on-site personnel Naples Fire did not require any action on their part.  Contaminated absorbant is being drummed and will be taken by Snelson.

name: Western Petroleum (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
Truck rollover caused release of 4,000 gallons of diesel fuel.  Is away from highways.  No waterways impacted.  Emergency response crew is enroute.  Coordinates will be given when determined.  
11:04 - PRP rep is onsite Pacific West is contractor enroute to remediate.  Spill occurred in a dry draw.  No inhibitive weather or rain.  Spilled off steep embankment on opposite side from access into the area.  Wash is est'd 400 yards across.  Access was made from Nine Mile road west of Miton, UT and about six miles beyond paved-unpaved demarcation.  Caller advised to notify NRC.

name: Natural Gas Release - Uintah Co.
incident_summary:
Caller is reporting a release of 7.66 Million cubic feet of natural gas from a valve that was open overnight.

The facility operator left at 10:00 PM Friday night and when a operator returned at 7:00 AM the next morning, they discovered the valve on the contactor tower was open.  

The valve company bypassed the valve to stop the release and is in the process of repairing the valve.

name: Uintah County Production Water Spill
incident_summary:
Caller reported that approximately 60 barrels of treated injection water leaked from a broken pipe and ran into a dry drainage.  Three to five barrels of this was production water, the rest was clean water.  They were able to recover approximately 40 barrels.  They are flushing the drainage with clean water and will take soil samples afterwards.

The leak occurred at well number 1-31-8-18.

There was no threat to surface or ground water.

name: Vernal - Hydraulic oil at Simplot
incident_summary:
Caller reported the release of 30 gallons hydraulic oil from a ruptured hydraulic line on a piece of machinery. Hydraulic oil released to the soils. Contaminated soils will be excavated. No surface waters were impacted.

Contact for Simplot is John Spencer (Simplot - Environmental Engineer) (435) 621-2629.

name: Duchesne County - Treated Injection Water Release
incident_summary: Caller reported a release due to internal corrosion of piping resulting in about 93 bbls of treated injection water.  The release was initiated from above the well site designated as 11-23-9-15 with coordinates of T9S R15E S23.  The release flowed down to the road and flowed over down to where it stopped at the berm located at the well site.  No waterways were impacted.  The line was repaired and cleanup is in progress.  The area will be flushed with fresh water after cleanup is completed likely later in the day.
title_eventname: Duchesne County - Treated Injection Water Release

name: Duchesne Co - Diesel 30 Gallons
incident_summary: 30 gallons of diesel fuel leaked from the saddle tanks on a logging truck.  Leak occurred about 200 yards from the Duchesne River.

name: Duchesne Co - Treated Injection Water
incident_summary: Caller is reporting a release of approximately 75 barrels of treated injection water.  Water origniated from right-of-way to off-location and spread out into an area of large open range for about 500 yards.  No surface drainages were impacted.  Caused by internal corrosion of the service line.  Crew has isolated the line and repairing.  PRP is determining course of remedial action.

name: Newton Gas (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary:
CALLER STATED THAT THERE IS A 2 INCH WATER INJECTION WATERLINE THAT BROKE
  AND RAN DOWN TOWARDS WATER INJECTON WELL NUMBER 8-26-8-16 LOCATION. CALLER STATED THAT THE  MATERIAL RAN DOWN THE ROAD AND BROKE THROUGH THE BERM ON THE
  LOCATION AND THEN WENT OFF THE LOCATION.  CALLER STATED THAT IT MADE
  IT OFF 100 YARDS OFF THE LOCATION AND SANK IN THE GROUND.  CALLER
  STATED THAT THE MATERIAL REACHED NO WATERWAY AND 150 BARRELS WAS THE
  TOTAL SPILL AND 50 BARRELS WENT OFF THE LOCATION.

name: Kerr-McGee (c/o haul Contractor to be determined) (Null RP Substituted)
responsible_party: Kerr-McGee (c/o haul Contractor to be determined)
incident_summary:
Tank truck delivered gas condensate ("60 gravity") to separation station tank at salt water disposal facility.   Operator closed valve and uncoupled effluent line from truck.  Kerr-McGee crew discovered that valve had not been closed 100% and secondary check valve failed enabling content to slowly drain.  Loss estimated at 40 barrels (42 gal/bbl).  Estimate 20-30 barrels left the location and flowed about to ephemeral stream channel 400 yards and stopped.  Channel is dry so condensate did not mix with any running water.  Caller dispatched a backhoe to construct secondary containment downstream of material as preventative measure in the event material is mobilized.  Will be checking log to determine attribtution.  Contaminated soils will be excavated and disposed at approved landfill.  Location is est. 47 miles south of Vernal.  White River is the downstream receptor.
UPDATE 4/27/07 DEQ DE reports that cleanup by Kerr McGee is going well.  Release was caused by faulty valve.  Agency representatives will return to perform a post-cleanup survey.
title_eventname: Kerr-McGee (c/o haul Contractor to be determined) (Null RP Substituted)

name: Duchesne Co - Treated Injection Water
incident_summary: Well Site Location 4-32-8-17.  Underground injection line broke and treated injection water flowed to nearby dry drainage.  Estimated volume 30 barrels.  Flushed with 500 bbls of fresh water.

name: EP EnergyRelease, near Duchesne
incident_summary: Caller reported the release of 49 barrels of produced water down a dry gulch.  Material has been adsorbed into the dirt.  Caller will contact District Engineer and DOGM.

name: Altamont - Propylene glycol spill
incident_summary: Caller reported a spill of 11 barrels (462 gallons) of propylene glycol to soil due to a break in a pipeline.  The contaminated soil was excavated and taken to a landfill.  No waterways were impacted.  Sampling was done to make sure that all the contaminated soil was excavated.  Caller reported this incident to Dennis Ingram at DOGM and Nathan Hall, DEQ District Engineer.

name: Rosevelt Top Stop Release
incident_summary: Release occurred at a Top-Stop facility.  PRP as identifed, was refueling both diesel saddle tanks on a tractor.  When driver discovered second line releasing he shut the line.  An estimated 25-60 gallons of diesel was released.  An estimated volume of thirty-one gallons flowed from the containment pad and entered a nearby creek.  Fire Dept responded.  Response crew has deployed booms and absorbents.  Contractor (Envirocare) out of Salt Lake has been mobilized (E.T.A. is several hours).

name: Utah Power & Light (Null RP Substituted)
incident_summary: Caller reported the release of 35 gallons non-PCB mineral oil from 2 transformers.  The transformers were mounted on a utility pole.  The pole had apparently rotted and strong overnight winds knocked the pole and the transformers down onto an asphalt parking area.  UP&L crews arrived on-scene to clean-up the released mineral oil.
